checks.name: defect-reproduced-over-http
checks.summary: A3, reproduced before the repair and kept in the tree as A7's permanent assertion. Against the composed api.Handler over real HTTP: a Requirement was captured through POST /v1/requirements as the owner, then POST /v1/requirements/{id}:request-input was sent as a RUNNER caller with a valid body naming the Requirement's actual current version. VERDICT: REFUSED. Status code 400. Error body VERBATIM from the run: {"correlation_id":"75ac35ecbc32870ecb29d8a5","error":"invalid_request","message":"invalid domain state transition","schema_version":"v1"}. The refusal is attributable to domain.ErrInvalidTransition and to nothing else: the body carries that error's exact text, the body was well-formed so it is not validation, the caller was a role the route accepts so 401 and 403 are excluded, and the expected version was the Requirement's actual version so 409 is excluded. The Requirement's status, its version and every other field were asserted byte-unchanged by the refusal with reflect.DeepEqual, and the needs-input side table was read directly and still held no row. This reproduction stays in the tree permanently so the precondition can never silently become reachable from captured.

checks.name: route-is-unambiguous-and-role-gated
checks.summary: A8. POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:start-framing added to internal/api/api.go's POST switch default branch, using the same prefix-plus-suffix idiom as the existing :request-input and :answer-input branches, with a named suffix constant startFramingSuffix beside requestInputSuffix and answerInputSuffix. Gated to RoleOwner or RoleScheduler. VERDICT: PASS, with the routing proved by assertion and not by reading. Measured: 401 unauthenticated; 403 for a runner caller; 404 for an empty requirement id; 404 for /v1/executions/{id}:start-framing, which is the direct proof that the execution-scoped :start branch does not claim this suffix in either direction, because :start-framing does not satisfy HasSuffix(path, ":start") and the executions branch is prefix-gated anyway; a GET to the very same path does NOT return 200, so it is not the framing route and the method-gated GET /v1/requirements/ prefix branch does not swallow the POST; 404 from the command for an unknown Requirement id; 409 for a stale expected version; and 400 for each of three smuggled body fields (control_revision, repository_id, at), which the strict decoder refuses rather than ignores. Every refusal left the Requirement byte-unchanged (reflect.DeepEqual). The owner call returned 200 with a response carrying exactly requirement_id, status and version, status framing, and the state moved in the store -- which is the proof that the POST reached the command rather than a read branch. A second framing with a FRESH request id returned 400 naming `invalid domain state transition` and left the Requirement byte-unchanged. The scheduler was accepted on its own Requirement, so the route gates exactly the pair the capture route gates.

checks.name: determinism-of-the-new-api-tests
checks.summary: A14's determinism clause for internal/api. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine was added. The new tests inject their own clock (framingClock) and step it forward EXPLICITLY between read transactions, for a measured reason rather than a stylistic one: a read transaction reserves the conservative read boundary (quota.ReadTransactionUsage, Reads 6001) against the daily budget, the in-memory adapter never trues that reservation up, and the daily counter resets on a UTC day change, so a fixed clock admits only four read transactions per store per day and the A10 chain performs more than four reads. Advancing an injected clock is not a wait and involves no timer; no walk and no assertion was weakened to avoid the limit. The one duration reported by the live-local run is logged as an observation and never asserted as a threshold, and the live-local test's own waits are its pre-existing bounded deadline polls (waitForHealthz), reused unchanged.
